input.quote: 22.14 Solicitation. Neither party shall solicit the employees of the other party during the Term of this Agreement, for any reason.
input.rationale: Section 22.14 binds us (as well as M&I) not to solicit any employee of the other party, for any reason, for the entire Term — a multi-year period given the 18-month renewal-notice mechanic in Section 2.2. That fails the fallback on three material terms: scope (all employees rather than personnel involved in the Services), duration (open-ended over the whole Term rather than 12 months from the end of involvement), and the absence of carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches. The redline keeps the clause mutual but narrows it to the fallback position with minimal edits.

proposal.summary: Narrow mutual non-solicit to personnel involved in the Services, 12 months, with customary carve-outs
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We narrowed this to the personnel actually involved in the Services and limited it to twelve months after their involvement ends, since a blanket bar on soliciting any employee for the whole Term is far broader than our playbook allows. We also added the customary carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches.

ops.oldText: Neither party shall solicit the employees of the other party during the Term of this Agreement, for any reason.
ops.newText: Neither party shall directly solicit for employment the employees of the other party who are directly involved in the performance or receipt of the Services, during the period of such involvement and for twelve (12) months thereafter. This Section does not restrict either party from making general solicitations for employment (including advertisements and searches by recruiting firms) not specifically directed at the other party's employees, or from hiring any person who responds to such a general solicitation or who approaches that party on an unsolicited basis.
